body.p: No novel is written alone, and this one depended on the generosity, expertise, and patience of many people.

My agent, Rachel Torres at Brightline Literary, saw the potential in a half-finished manuscript about a talking computer and fought for it with the tenacity of someone who genuinely believes in the power of stories to change minds. This book would not exist without her.

My editor, James Hargrove at Apex Fiction Press, pushed me to make the science sharper and the characters deeper, often in the same sentence. Every writer should be lucky enough to work with someone who cares this much about getting it right.

For the technical foundations, I am indebted to several researchers who reviewed early drafts and corrected my most egregious oversimplifications: Dr. Priya Krishnan (Stanford HAI), Dr. Marcus Webb (DeepMind), and Dr. Aisha Okonkwo (MIT CSAIL). Any remaining errors are mine, not theirs.
My writing group — Tom, Elena, Yuki, Liam, and Amara — provided invaluable feedback on every chapter. Yes, I borrowed your names. Yes, it's too late to change them.
My parents, Robert and Linda Mitchell, who gave me my first computer at age nine and never once told me to turn it off and go outside. Look what happened.
